examples.title: Anika Wells accused of treating voters like ‘3-year-olds’ after using Ooshies to explain housing crisis
examples.summary: Communications Minister Anika Wells is facing backlash for using Ooshies to explain Australia's housing crisis, with some likening her explanation to 'treating voters like 3-year-olds'. The minister's attempt to engage audiences on social media has been defended by some, but others find it infantilising. The housing affordability crisis remains a pressing issue in Australia.

examples.title: Unions unveil plans to extend standard lease agreements and increase public housing amid crisis
examples.summary: The Australian Council of Trade Unions is pushing for a national standard requiring landlords to offer tenants at least two years of housing security, amid the housing crisis. The proposal also includes stronger protections against unfair evictions and rent gouging. The ACTU is calling for a major public housing boost, aiming for 6% of Australia's total housing stock to be public housing.

examples.title: Housing market eased 'more than anticipated', RBA says
examples.summary: Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock says the world has become more shock-prone in recent years, with the latest spike in oil prices adding to monetary policy challenges.

examples.title: Why are Sydney house prices falling in some areas, but rising in others?
examples.summary: Sydney house prices are experiencing a downturn, with some areas seeing a 3.3% drop in the last quarter. However, other areas, such as outer suburbs, are still rising in price. Experts say the downturn is affecting premium locations first, but may eventually spread to more affordable areas.

examples.title: Melbourne suburbs among the most mortgage-stressed in Australia
examples.summary: Melbourne suburbs are among the most mortgage-stressed in Australia, with a doubling of calls for assistance from Mortgage Stress Victoria.

examples.title: ‘If you make $1250, you’ll pay $1850 tax bill’
examples.summary: Australia's new capital gains tax rules could drive investment away from the country, according to a finance expert.

examples.title: Major bank spells nightmare for investors
examples.summary: Major bank NAB has adjusted its house price forecast for Sydney and Melbourne, warning prices could plummet by 10 per cent due to a broad-based weakening of the market.

examples.title: ‘Enough is enough’: Woman’s defiant act
examples.summary: A woman, Chantell Vesuna, 31, from Melbourne, received financial help from her parents to buy her first home, highlighting the growing trend of family support in the Australian housing market.

examples.title: Who had it worse? The hidden shift behind Australia’s generational mortgage debate - SBS
examples.summary: New research from KPMG shows that households in Australia are facing greater mortgage pressure now than during the late 1980s, when interest rates reached 17.5%.

examples.title: The city defying Australia's housing slump — and why sellers are still reaping record gains - SBS
examples.summary: Darwin is the only capital city in Australia to record monthly home price growth, rising 0.2% in June, while the rest of the country saw a 0.3% decline in national home prices. Experts say cooling investor demand is giving first-home buyers more bargaining power, and the city's affordability is helping protect it against dips.

examples.title: Housing downturn accelerates, oil prices fall - SBS
examples.summary: Australia's property market is experiencing a downturn, with national property prices falling 0.7% in July, according to Cotality data. Oil prices also fell more than 5% due to Donald Trump's decision to call off planned strikes on Iran.

examples.title: How far property prices fell in the past – and how this year compares
examples.summary: Property prices have fallen by more than 3.5% in Sydney and Melbourne since the property downturn began, with experts warning the trend could have longer to run.

examples.title: If you want to understand why houses are so expensive, go to the airport
examples.summary: The article discusses the similarities between Australia's housing market and airport food prices, citing 'inelastic' demand and 'captive markets' as contributing factors. The article suggests that both housing and airport food prices are driven by limited supply and high costs, making it difficult for consumers to find alternatives. The article concludes that house prices can be reduced through policy changes, but airport food prices are likely to remain high due to their unique market dynamics.

examples.title: Sydney real estate auctions: First home buyers pay $2.33m for north shore house with a gazebo
examples.summary: First home buyers in Sydney are paying high prices for houses, with one buyer paying $2.33m for a north shore house. The Sydney property market is still sluggish, but clearance rates are showing signs of improvement. The article reports on two auctions where buyers paid above the reserve price, and experts say the market is slowly recovering.

examples.title: ‘Beyond reach’: Sydney’s owner-occupier rate slumps to 70-year low - theage.com.au
examples.summary: Sydney's owner-occupier rate has fallen to a 70-year low of 59.9% in 2025, with the city's median house price rising from $646,000 to $1.79m since 2011.

examples.title: Australian real estate: Buckle up for the banks’ mortgage war! Home loans have fallen off a cliff - theage.com.au
examples.summary: Australian home loan applications have fallen by 15% in the June quarter, with some banks cutting interest rates to woo customers. The decline is attributed to the Reserve Bank's interest rate rises and the federal budget tax policy. The government's tax changes have also discouraged would-be first home buyers, with their mortgage applications down 23%.

examples.title: Architect-designed Sydney home fetches $12m, defying weak auction market - theage.com.au
examples.summary: A mid-century modern home in Sydney's Hunters Hill sold for $12 million in a fast auction, defying the weak auction market. The result is marginally higher than last week's preliminary clearance rate of 49 per cent. The home's price guide was $11 million, and it attracted three registered bidders. The sellers are hoping to downsize.

examples.title: Property prices are plunging in almost every capital city across Australia – see how your suburb rates
examples.summary: Property prices are falling in almost every suburb in Australia's biggest cities, with values dropping faster in Brisbane than Sydney.

examples.title: Further interest rate hikes could ‘devastate’ property market without easing unaffordability
examples.summary: Experts warn that further interest rate hikes could devastate the property market, leaving housing unaffordable.

examples.title: Amanda Rishworth and Nat Barr clash over tradie ranking in skilled migration scheme
examples.summary: Employment Minister Amanda Rishworth refused to say whether tradies should be prioritised over economists and animal trainers in Australia's skilled migration scheme, despite the country's housing crisis.

examples.title: Pauline Hanson meets with UK far-right figure Tommy Robinson
examples.summary: Pauline Hanson has met with UK far-right figure Tommy Robinson to record a podcast interview.

examples.title: The Issue Podcast: Demographer says the tax system is ‘unfair’ for families amid the great population debate
examples.summary: Demographer Professor Peter McDonald says the tax system is 'unfair' for families, and the Albanese Government should support families with children. The current system is income-tested and capped, while the Coalition proposes income splitting to reduce tax paid by couples. The Labor Government aims to reduce annual net overseas migration to 225,000 by 2027-28.

examples.title: How Pauline Hanson's winning the migration debate
examples.summary: New polling shows more Australians prefer Pauline Hanson's stance on immigration than that of either of the major parties.

examples.title: The 30-year policy collision behind Australia's housing crunch
examples.summary: The article discusses how a 30-year policy collision between the regulation of housing and the effective deregulation of migration in Australia has led to the country's housing affordability crisis. The collision began under the Howard government in the early 2000s, with the deregulation of migration and the regulation of construction. The article highlights how this policy collision has resulted in an explosion of net overseas migration, a shortage of construction trades, and a housing market that is unable to keep up with demand.

examples.title: Labor was poised to reveal massive migration cuts, then suddenly delayed
examples.summary: Australia's Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has postponed a speech on migration changes, citing unfinalized details.

examples.title: ‘Wild’: Shock as Aussie visa fees skyrocket
examples.summary: Australia has increased visa fees for students, backpackers, and Kiwis by nearly 200% for international students and 25% for most visa applications, sparking criticism from experts and the business community. The increases come into effect this week.

examples.title: ‘Tank the economy’: One Nation alert
examples.summary: One Nation's plan to slash immigration by 750,000 over three years would 'tank the Australian economy' on a scale not seen since the 1890s Depression, a prominent political commentator warns.

examples.title: Inside Narendra Modi's Australia visit: Optics are warm. Politics are harder
examples.summary: The article discusses the upcoming visit of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Australia, highlighting the complexities of their relationship and the challenges that come with it. Modi's visit is expected to focus on delivery, with experts saying it will test whether the close relationship between Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Modi can translate into concrete outcomes. The article also touches on the sensitive issues of agriculture, defence, and migration, as well as the human rights concerns surrounding Modi's government.

examples.title: The competing visions for Australia's migration system
examples.summary: The Australian government has unveiled its long-awaited migration reforms, aiming to reduce net overseas migration and address housing pressures. The reforms include changes to the points test, visa overstayers, and international students. examples.title: Labor recruits ex-Liberal premier to champion multiculturalism
examples.summary: Labor has appointed former Liberal premier Peter Gutwein as chair of Australia's peak multicultural advisory council, warning that rhetoric from the right is fuelling hatred and vilification. The appointment comes amid fierce debate on the political right over multiculturalism. Gutwein said Australia had benefited from decades of bipartisan support for multiculturalism and that such an approach provided certainty and confidence in the system. He also warned that the leaning towards the right was very unhelpful and needed to be called out. The council's work helps ensure that people of all backgrounds feel valued, connected and able to contribute to Australia's future.

examples.title: ‘Could see myself sitting here’: One Nation MP Farley gatecrashes Liberal meeting
examples.summary: One Nation MP David Farley gatecrashed a private meeting of Liberal MPs and made a comment about sitting with them, sparking speculation about his future in the party.

examples.title: One Nation denies fringe influencer is a member after he supports neo-Nazi rights
examples.summary: One Nation party denies membership of influencer Andre Mamet after he defends neo-Nazi views

examples.title: Labor pushes to boost Pacific workers as Joyce says some Australians ‘bung lazy’
examples.summary: Labor is pushing to boost Pacific workers as part of its migration plan, while One Nation and industries warn that cuts to working holidaymakers will cripple regional operations.

examples.title: Migration fix could hit parliament next week – but these sticking points remain
examples.summary: The Australian government is close to announcing a new migration policy, but talks between Labor and the Coalition remain stuck on key issues. The policy aims to reduce the net overseas migration figure from 300,000 to 225,000. The Greens are unlikely to support any reduction in migration, and the Coalition has set 10 red lines for any legislation, including making it illegal to repatriate ISIS families.

examples.title: ‘A big chunk of positive energy’: Green Man celebrates 10 years of training refugees
examples.summary: Green Man festival in Wales has been extending its formative experience to refugees and asylum seekers through a 10-year-old training programme.

examples.title: Israeli siblings who fear breaking law in Gaza under IDF owed protection by Australia, tribunal finds
examples.summary: A tribunal in Australia has found that three Israeli siblings who fear breaking international humanitarian law in Gaza should be afforded protection visas.

differences.description: 7NEWS focuses on policy process, security, morality, and economic consequences, while ABC News covers policy process, human interest, conflict, security, and economic consequences.
ABC News covers human interest, conflict, security, and economic consequences, while News.com.au focuses on economic consequences and policy process.
SBS News covers policy process, while Sydney Morning Herald covers policy process, conflict, security, economic consequences, and human interest.
The Age covers economic consequences and conflict, while The Guardian Australia covers human interest and policy process.

examples.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has announced funding for a solar battery project in Palau, while defending the country's investment in a pre-COP climate conference in Fiji and Tuvalu.

examples.title: Batteries now cheaper than gas for peak demand power supply
examples.summary: Batteries are now cheaper than gas for peak demand power supply, according to a report by the CSIRO.

examples.title: Australia's green energy targets in 'jeopardy' as wind woes worsen

examples.summary: The National Press Club of Australia hosted a series of addresses by various politicians, experts, and industry leaders on various topics including the economy, climate change, healthcare, and foreign policy.

examples.title: Mega battery threatens beloved Sydney site

examples.title: What happens when coal mines close and renewable energy takes over? - SBS
examples.summary: Renewable energy is taking over coal mines in New South Wales, with a focus on grid-scale batteries. The Hunter region is expected to lose 12,000 jobs when coal mines close in 2030. Local residents are optimistic about the transition, but concerned about the impact on their community.

examples.title: Tomago Smelter gets $2.5 billion bail-out - SBS
examples.summary: New South Wales and the Commonwealth Government have agreed to provide a $2.5 billion bailout for the Tomago Aluminium Smelter over ten years.

examples.title: ClearVue recruits world-leading solar glass expert
examples.summary: ClearVue Technologies appoints Professor Rebecca Yang as an independent non-executive director, bringing expertise in BIPV and sustainable building technologies.

examples.summary: Danish investment giant Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners has acquired the Gawara Baya wind farm in North Queensland, providing a much-needed boost to Australia's renewable energy ambitions.

examples.title: Critica bolsters ranks for dual critical minerals push
examples.summary: Critica bolsters ranks for dual critical minerals push, with the appointment of experienced minerals engineer Mike Kevan as interim study manager, as the company progresses parallel studies on two major scoping studies. The company aims to strengthen its technical capability and build a scalable Australian critical minerals platform. The Mt Lindsay tin-tungsten project and the Jupiter rare earths project are expected to be completed in the third quarter of 2026.

examples.title: Green energy giants see $155b data centre boom as win for net zero
examples.summary: Major renewable energy investors support Australia's data centre boom, while community and environmental campaigners express concerns about the power-hungry facilities.

examples.title: ‘Disillusioned’ customers discover the catch in three hours of free power
examples.summary: Australians may face higher electricity bills after signing up for the government's Solar Sharer program, which provides three hours of free power daily.

examples.title: Coal plants would cut power costs by 2050, but with a massive price to pay
examples.summary: The CSIRO says investing in more fossil fuels and limiting wind and solar farms could cut 5% off the cost of running Australia's electricity grid by 2050, but at the cost of abandoning climate commitments and increasing atmospheric pollution.

examples.title: Fuel on the fire: why oil companies are profiting as the world gets dangerously hot | Extreme heat
examples.summary: Oil companies are increasing production despite the dangers of climate change, with some companies aiming to increase production by 14% between 2024 and 2030.

examples.title: The climate fight has one great ally. You just can’t look at it directly | Bill McKibben
examples.summary: Climate experts and advocates are urging a rapid acceleration of clean energy to combat global warming. A group of leading advocates will deliver a letter to the UN, calling for clean energy access for everyone, everywhere by 2030.

examples.title: Coalition and One Nation’s plan to ditch net zero would not lower power prices, CSIRO report finds
examples.summary: A CSIRO report finds that abandoning a net zero climate target would not lower power prices, and that nuclear power would be the most expensive option for electricity generation in Australia.

clean_energy.overview: The media framing app analyzed the coverage of clean energy topics across various news outlets. The analysis found that the outlets tend to focus on economic consequences, policy processes, and security aspects of clean energy. The outlets also cover human-interest stories, conflict, and responsibility-related topics. The analysis highlights the importance of considering the different frames and perspectives presented by various news outlets when discussing clean energy topics.

outlet_patterns.pattern: ABC News tends to focus on economic consequences and policy processes of clean energy. The outlet also covers security aspects and human-interest stories.
Sydney Morning Herald tends to focus on economic consequences and conflict related to clean energy. The outlet also covers security aspects and responsibility-related topics.
The Guardian Australia tends to focus on security and conflict related to clean energy. The outlet also covers policy processes and economic consequences.
